correctness.rationale: For odd N, the core unanimously follows the initial majority M. A peripheral vertex follows the core's prevailing sign when 2X<c-1 or 2X>c+1 and keeps its own bit otherwise. In the keep-bit regime moving the c core bits to M cannot reverse the original majority. Hence c>ell rules out reversal, and for ell>c the low-core/high-total event is X<=floor((c-2)/2), X+Y> N/2, with its complementary counterpart. The joint binomial CLT gives correlation sqrt(c/N); the exceptional at-most-two core counts have probability O(c^(-1/2)), and the Gaussian angular measure gives arccos(1/sqrt(1+rho))/pi for finite rho>=1. One quarter is a limit, not a finite-system equality. The independent replay `python3 /workspace/reproduce.py` exhaustively checked 114408 labeled profiles and verified the (10,11) example separately. That computation does not prove the limit.
